column3: The Hebrew says heart and heart; BSB says a double heart.
The Hebrew has a singular tongue speaking great things without an explicit every.
The Hebrew has a singular tongue and says our lips are with us; BSB says tongues and we own our lips.
The Hebrew mentions refined silver and purification sevenfold, without separately naming gold, which BSB adds.
The Hebrew first says them, then him; BSB says us in both clauses.
The Hebrew links the clauses with when; BSB uses and.
